question: Athar can do a certain work in the same time in which Baban and Chetan together can do it. If Athar and Baban together could do it in 10 days and Chetan alone in 50 days, then Baban alone could do it in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(10, 50) = 50 units.

Efficiency of (Athar + Baban) = 5 units/day, Chetan = 1 unit/day.

Since Athar = Baban + Chetan, replacing Athar gives: 2 × Baban + Chetan = 5.

2 × Baban + 1 = 5 ⇒ Baban's efficiency = 2 units/day.

Time taken by Baban alone = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Athar takes the same time as Baban and Chetan together.

⇒ Efficiency of Athar (A) = Efficiency of Baban (B) + Efficiency of Chetan (C)

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = B + C

⇒ Combined efficiency: A + B = 5

⇒ Substituting A = B + C in the combined efficiency equation:

⇒ (B + C) + B = 5

⇒ 2B + C = 5

⇒ Since C's efficiency is 1:

⇒ 2B + 1 = 5 ⇒ 2B = 4

⇒ B = 2 units/day

⇒ Time taken by Baban alone = Total Work ÷ B's Efficiency = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 days

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work using LCM

Total work is generally assumed as the LCM of all the given time periods. This makes the one-day work (efficiency) an integer value, making calculation easier.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the direct proportion of the amount of work done by each individual. If they work for the same duration, wages are split in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

The core concept remains exactly the same as Time & Work, with the only difference being that a leak or emptying pipe has negative efficiency.
